editorial:
Imagine you and your best friends are heading to a huge music festival in Texas, totally hyped for the weekend. Your car breaks down, and just when you think you are stuck, a friendly guy in a cool van pulls over to give you a lift. He seems great at first, but the vibe shifts fast. Once you get deep into the lonely Texas backroads, your friends start disappearing one by one. You realize you are not just hitching a ride; you are trapped in a game where the driver is the one in control, and your only goal is to get out alive before the music even starts.

The acting is top-notch, especially the guy playing the driver who manages to be creepy and charming at the same time. The movie moves quickly and keeps you guessing with a few big surprises that you won't see coming. Some parts feel a bit predictable, but the tension makes up for it.
endingExplained: In the final act, you find out the driver is actually a serial killer who collects people as trophies for his secret basement. The last survivor manages to trick him during a fight in the van, causing it to crash into a ditch. After a brutal struggle, the survivor kills the driver with his own trophy knife and walks toward a nearby gas station just as the sun comes up, finally escaping the nightmare.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves survival stories and creepy strangers.
